  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE LA VERNE PLANNING COMMISSION
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9, 2025

  ACTION MINUTES

REGULAR MEETING - 6:30 p.m. - Chairperson Simison called the meettng called to order at
6:30 p.m.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE - Led by Commissioner Duffy

ROLL CALL  Commissioner Keny Chang, Commissioner Jeremy Conrad, Commissioner
  Erin Duffy, Vice-Chairperson Thomas Allison, and Chairperson Jason
  Simison.

Commissioners present: Simison, Allison, Conrad, and Duffi
Absent: Chang (aruived at 6:33pm)
Advisory Staff Present: Community Development Director Eric Scherer, Principal Planner
Candice Bowcock, Assistant City Attorney Lisa Kranitz, and Assistant Planner Valerie Chin.

MINUTES - February 12,2025 - It was moved by Commissioner Duffy and seconded by
Commissioner Conrad to approve the minutes of the February 12, 2025 meeting. The motion
carried by a 4-0 vote.

Commissioner Chang entered the room at 6:3jpm

PUBLIC COMMENT - None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

Project: Case Numbers 28-25CUP and 29-25GUP - 2330 Foothill Boulevard - Conditional
Use Permit to allow the operation of a Trader Joe's grocery store with Type 21 license
for off-site sale of alcoholic beverages

RECOMMENDATION:
On April l, 2025, based on staff's recommendation, the Development Review Committee
 "DRC") recommended that the Planning Commtssion approve Case Nos. 28-25CUP and 29-
25CUP and adopt Resolutton No. 1335 (Attachment l) and Resolution No. 1336 (Auachment 2)
based on the staffreport presented to them, and thefindings and conditions of approval. Since
the time that the staffreport was presented to the DRC, staffhas determined that the subject
property is not considered adjacent to residential use. Accordingly, staffis removing the
conditions of approval that will restrict the loading and unloading hours and recycling pick up
hours to specific times.

Presentation: Assistant Planner Chin made a presentation to the Planning Commission going
over the recommendation and staff report that was part of the agenda packet.
  Public Comments: None

 Commissioner Comments: All Commissioners stated they are hoppy to see Trader Joe's coming
 to the City of La Verne.

It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner Drffy to approve
Resolution No. 1335 to approve a CUP for a market. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner Duffy to approve
Resolution No. 1336. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

Project: Case No. 26-25GUP - 968 Palomares Avenue - Gonditionat Use Permit to allow
the operation of an indoor private training facility (The Forge)

 RECOMMENDATION:
 On April I, 2025, based on staff's recommendation, the Development Review Committee
  "DRC") recommended that the Planning Commission approve Case No. 26-25CUP and adopt
 Resolution No. 1334 (Attachment l) based on the staffreport presented to them, and the
findings and conditions of approval. Since the time that the staff report was presented to the
 DRC, it has come to staff's attention that the state law relied upon in that report to exempt the
 business from additional parking does not apply to this project. Accordingly, staff is inciuding a
 condition of approval that will limit the number of occupants at any given time based on the
 number of avatlable parking spaces.

Presentation: Assistant Planner Chin made a presentation to the Planning Commission going
over the recommendation and staff report that was part of the agenda packet.

 Commissioner Comments: Commissioner Conrad askedfor clarification of the letter received
from the property owner and Assistant Planner Chin clarified that the property owner is in
 support of the business as long as they adhere to the conditions of approval. Commissioner
 Chang asked if the clients are by appoinfinent only and the applicant answered, yes.
 Commissioner Dufy stated she had no concerns. Commissioner Allison asked about parking
 and possibly staggering the reserttation times. Chairperson Simison stated he has no concerns.

Public Comments: The applicant, Sunny Soohoo, explained their business model and said they
would stagger reservation times to be sure that parking will not be a problem.

Loddy Chao, the property owner, also spoke and explained there is not currently a parking
problem.

Community Development Director Scherer stated that the conditions of approval will allow the
City to regulate the parking concerns.

It was moved by Commissioner Drffy and seconded by Commissioner Conrad to approve
Resolutton No. I334. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

Project: Case Number 43-19CUP - 2855 Foothil! Boulevard - Revocation of Conditiona!
use Permit for the operation of a massage establishment - platinum spa

  t>.t2r'214
  RECOMMENDATION:
 Staffrecommends the Planning Commission revoke the Conditional Use Permit (Case No. 43-
 I ?CUP) approved under Resolution No. I 3 37 allowing the operation of a massage
 establishment (Platinum Spa) located at 2855 Foothill Boulevard (Attachment l). Assistant City
Attorney Kranitz clarifiedfor the Commission that the revocation of the CUP is not specifically
for Platinum Spa, but for any other massage business that would want to operate there.

Presentation: Principal Planner Bowcock made a presentation to the Commission going over
the staff report and recommendation that was part of the agenda.

Public Comments: Paul Cha, owner of Platinum Spa, spoke about how hewas unaware about
what was happening in the business and that he never met the person that was arrested and the
Manager that hired her had vanished. He said that the person had only worked there that day
that she was arrested and asked that the Planning Commission delay any decision until she had
her day in court. He said that due process was not being provided to him. He indicated he can't
control what people do, also referring to Principal Planner Bowcock and that he can't control
what she does after work. He indicated that he has $140,000 invested into the business and that
the Landlord was trying to bleed him dry.

No other comments were received.

Commissioner Allison said he disagreed with the owner and that as the owner of the business it
is his responsibility to lmow what happens there. He said that it was clearfrom the reviews on
Yelp that this had been going onfor years.

Commissioner Duffy clarified that they were not making a decision on his business but the
CUP. She indicated that it was clear that there was systematic prostitution happening at the
location and was a public nuisance to the community. Shefurther stated her concerns that if the
CUP was not revoked and another massage business opened up, then those same customers
would come back.

Commissioner Chang agreed with Commissioners Allison and Duffy andfurther stated that the
business owner is the one who is responsiblefor lcnowing what happens there. He was
concerned because there are residential units and children in the same complex as the business.

Commissioner Conrad said that he appreciated the other Commissioners' comments and that as
he himself is a small business owner, he is liablefor what happens. He stated that continuing to
allow for massage at this location will just continue a pattern and put others at risk. He stated
that if the La Verne Police Department and the Sherriff did a sting operation, it shows that there
was a pattern.

Chairperson Simison said that all of the Commissioners made good points and that he did not
have anything else to add.

It was moved by Commisstoner Conrad and seconded by Chairperson Simison to approve
Resolution No. 1337, revoking Case No. 43-l?CUPfor a massage establishment permit. Motion
carried by a 5-0 vote.

PLANNING COMMISSIONER COMMENTS _

Commissioner Conrad said that it is great to see new businesses coming into La Verne.
  Paee 314
 Commissioner Chang asked if staffregularly conducted inspections on businesses. Director
Scherer indicated that there are unannounced inspections done by our Police Department and
Planning Staff to the massage business. Otherwise, typically only the Fire Department conducts
annual inspections of all businesses.

Commissioner Allison said that it is a privilege to do business

Chairperson Simison thanked stafffor all of their hard work.

DIRECTOR COMMENTS -

Director Schererformally welcomed AssistantCity Attorney Kranitz to the Planning
Commission, explaining that Deputy City Attorney Porter had been selected as the-City
Attorneyfor another agency and no longer would have time to serve the Commission. Director
Scherer also welcomed Planning Intern Kaitlyn Cavan to the Department and stated that there
is a needfor the May l4th meeting.

ADJOURNMENT - The meeting was adjourned at 7:33 p.m.
